questions.q: What does a `type: ALL` value in EXPLAIN output indicate, per this lesson?
options: A full table scan — MySQL examines every row, the access type to watch for
MySQL is using the best possible index lookup
The query returned zero rows
The table has no primary key defined
questions.explain: type is ordered roughly best to worst, and ALL means a full table scan, the access type to be most concerned about on a sizable table.

questions.q: Why is the `key` column often described as one of the most informative in this lesson?
options: It shows which index MySQL actually used, and NULL on a table you expected to be indexed is a direct signal of a problem
It always matches the table's primary key column name
It lists every index that exists on the table, used or not
It shows the number of rows returned by the query
questions.explain: key reveals the actual index chosen (or none, if NULL), making it a fast way to spot a missing or unused index.

questions.q: What does "Using filesort" in the Extra column mean, per this lesson?
options: MySQL needs an extra pass to sort the result set because it couldn't use an index to produce rows in the required order
MySQL is writing the entire result set to a text file on disk
The query has a syntax error related to file paths
MySQL skipped sorting entirely for performance
questions.explain: Using filesort signals an extra sorting step (not necessarily on disk) because no index satisfied the ORDER BY directly.

questions.q: What does "Using temporary" in the Extra column typically indicate, per this lesson?
options: MySQL needs to build a temporary table to complete the query, often seen with certain GROUP BY or DISTINCT patterns
The query is using a temporary, non-persistent table as its data source
MySQL failed to execute the query and used a fallback
The index used is scheduled for deletion
questions.explain: Using temporary signals MySQL needed a temp table, commonly for GROUP BY/DISTINCT patterns that can't be satisfied directly from an index.

questions.q: Why is "Using index" in the Extra column considered a good sign, per this lesson?
options: It means the query is satisfied entirely from the index itself without touching the underlying table data
It means the query used every available index on the table
It means indexing was disabled for that query, speeding it up
It always means the query returned exactly one row
questions.explain: Using index describes a covering index scenario, which avoids reading table rows and is faster than a typical index lookup.
